name: Directory Of Unsheltered Street Homeless To General Population Ratio 2011
description:
This dataset lists eight major U.S. cities and, for each, gives the 2011 count of people experiencing unsheltered street homelessness, the city's general population, and the resulting ratio of unsheltered homeless residents to the overall population (expressed as "1 in N"). Cities include Washington, DC, Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York City, and Chicago, among others. Counts range from a few hundred to roughly 15,770 unsheltered individuals, and general populations range from about 433,000 to more than 8 million.

The data can be used to compare the prevalence of street homelessness across cities of very different sizes, since the ratio normalizes for population. It supports advocacy, policy analysis, and funding decisions, and provides a 2011 baseline for tracking how unsheltered homelessness changes over time. Because the table is small, it is best suited to simple comparisons and illustrative analysis rather than statistical modeling.
